faq.v: Which walking route is closest to the hotel?
faq.a: The Boshuizerbergen near Smakt, a few minutes' drive away. There you walk 5.5 kilometres past thousands of junipers, pine forest and open drift sand.

faq.v: Can I get walking routes at reception?
faq.a: Yes. Free walking and cycling routes on paper are available at reception. Every route on this page also opens on your phone, with the button next to the route.

faq.v: Can I take a packed lunch with me?
faq.a: Yes. You can order a packed lunch for the road at reception.

faq.v: Can I eat at the hotel after my walk?
faq.a: Yes. You are welcome to join us for dinner in our restaurant; the kitchen is open until 9.30 pm.

faq.v: Do I need a car to get to the starting point?
faq.a: Not always. The Boshuizerbergen and Landgoed Geijsteren are within cycling distance, and you can hire a bike or e-bike at reception. For the Maasduinen and the Mariapeel you take the car: a fifteen to thirty minute drive.

boshuizerbergen.alt: A couple taking a selfie on a wide forest path in the woods near Venray
boshuizerbergen.tekst: Near Smakt you follow the white route of Het Limburgs Landschap: 5.5 kilometres past the largest juniper scrub in the southern Netherlands, planted pine forest and stretches of open drift sand. Sheep keep the sand and heath open, so your dog stays on the lead. The threat of this area being cultivated led to the founding of Het Limburgs Landschap in 1931.

landgoed-geijsteren.alt: A forest path on Landgoed Geijsteren with the Willibrorduskapel among the trees
landgoed-geijsteren.tekst: Landgoed Geijsteren has belonged to the same family since 1806. The 7.7 kilometre loop follows the walking junctions along the Oostrumse Beek, a stream that was never straightened here, and passes the De Rosmolen watermill and the Willibrorduskapel. The paths are mostly unpaved, so wear good shoes.

alts.fotos/l26-route-landgoed-geijsteren-1.we: Meadow and woodland by the Oostrumse Beek on Landgoed Geijsteren

maasheggen.alt: A sandy path between hedges and trees in the hedge landscape along the Maas
maasheggen.tekst: Just over a fifteen minute drive away lies Sambeek, on the edge of the Maasheggen: since 2018 the only UNESCO biosphere reserve in the Netherlands. The 4.3 kilometre Rondje Heg en Maas starts at the weir and lock complex and follows the junctions along field paths and between the hedges. Keep your distance from the livestock in the meadows.

alts.fotos/l26-route-maasheggen-2.webp: Meadows bordered by hedges and trees in the Maasheggen, seen from above

ballonzuilbossen.alt: The Ballonzuil monument in the Ballonzuilbossen near Merselo
ballonzuilbossen.tekst: The Ballonzuilbossen near Merselo cover more than 260 hectares of mixed woodland on former raised bog; from 1906 the first forest of Venray was planted here. The 5 kilometre nature walk passes the Ballonzuil, the monument to the balloon from besieged Paris that landed near Merselo in the winter of 1871.

pieterpad-vierlingsbeek-swolgen.alt: A couple standing close together taking a photo on a sandy path through the autumn woods
pieterpad-vierlingsbeek-swolgen.tekst: A day's walk on the Pieterpad, marked in red and white: 24 kilometres from Vierlingsbeek station to the church in Swolgen. The trail passes close to Venray, through the Boshuizerbergen and across Landgoed Geijsteren, and continues via Wanssum and Meerlo. It is not a loop, so plan in advance how you will get back.

maasduinen-bij-bergen.alt: A wooden bench beside a path through the heath in the late sunlight
maasduinen-bij-bergen.tekst: Almost 10 kilometres through woods and heath in the north of De Maasduinen National Park, near Bergen. Groundwater is pumped up here for the drinking water of Bergen and parts of Gennep and Venlo, so stay on the paths and take your litter home with you.

lekkerbekkenroute.alt: Pools and heath in De Maasduinen National Park
lekkerbekkenroute.tekst: A route for food lovers over the rolling paths of De Maasduinen National Park: past a pancake house, a stretch along the Maas and on to the Hertog Jan Brouwerij in Arcen. The dunes themselves formed in the last ice age from wind-blown river sand.

rondje-mariaveen.alt: A wooden bridge over a canal near Helenaveen
rondje-mariaveen.tekst: You start in Helenaveen, which with Griendtsveen is one of the two peat colonies of the southern Netherlands and a protected village. The route leads through the Mariaveen, where peat cutting left behind canals, peat pits and pools. Purple moor grass and heather grow on the open plains.

wandelen-door-de-mariapeel.alt: Birches and heath by the water in the Mariapeel
wandelen-door-de-mariapeel.tekst: From Helenaveen you walk along the Helenavaart, the small canal used to carry peat into the twentieth century, into the Mariapeel. The raised bog here has kept its original character, and a herd of Dutch landrace goats grazes on the heath. Wear waterproof shoes.
